Severe Incidence and Mortality

severe-mortality.Rmd

A note of severity and mortality parameters and modelling:

The parameters used here to model severe incidence and mortality are highly uncertain and will vary geographically and with time. The default parameters are fit to data and represent our best current estimates, but should be considered carefully in use.

This vignette focuses on the methodology. For a runnable, end-to-end example of producing rates (including severe incidence and mortality) from a simulation, see the vignette("analysing_malaria_output").

Severe incidence

Postie first makes an adjustment to the incidence of severe cases output from malariasimulation. We now assume that early treatment of clinical cases can prevent a subset of those cases from becoming severe.

We use:

  • severe incidence from malariasimulation (sms_{m}), which is the modelled incidence of hospitalised severe cases,

  • the treatment coverage, set in malariasimulation (txt_x),

  • the proportion of severe cases averted by early treatment (ν\nu, default: 42% [1]),

  • a baseline treatment coverage (f0f_0, default: 10%) — the treatment coverage assumed when the severe model was originally fitted in Griffin et al (2016),

  • and a reference hospitalisation proportion (ρ0=0.8\rho_0 = 0.8) used in that original fit.

Among the treated fraction of cases (txt_x) a proportion ν\nu of severe cases is averted, leaving (1−ν)(1 - \nu). Because the modelled severe output corresponds to the baseline coverage f0f_0, the treatment adjustment is expressed relative to that baseline, following the Griffin et al (2016) SI. We also convert the modelled hospitalised severe incidence to total severe incidence using the reference hospitalisation proportion ρ0\rho_0. The postie (total) severe incidence is then:

sp=smρ0⋅(1−ν)tx+(1−tx)(1−ν)f0+(1−f0) s_p = \frac{s_m}{\rho_0} \cdot \frac{(1 - \nu)\,t_x + (1 - t_x)}{(1 - \nu)\,f_0 + (1 - f_0)}

ν\nu can be adjusted with the treatment_scaler argument in the get_rates() function of postie. The baseline coverage f0f_0 and reference hospitalisation ρ0\rho_0 are fixed internally so that results stay consistent with the original Griffin (2016) calibration (and recover the original 0.215 deaths-to-hospitalised-severe ratio when the defaults are used).

Mortality

We can then calculate mortality based on:

  • the adjusted severe incidence (sps_p),

  • the probability of hospitalisation of a severe case (ρ\rho: 80% default [2])

  • the case fatality ratio of hospitalised severe cases (μH\mu_H: default = 6.5% [2-3])

  • and the case fatality ratio of non-hospitalised (community) severe cases (μC\mu_C: default = 60% [2, 4]).

mp=sp(ρμH+(1−ρ)μC) m_p = s_p ( \rho \mu_H + (1-\rho) \mu_C)

These three parameters can also be adjusted. An adjusted ρ\rho must be set as a column named ft_sev in the malariasimulation object, which can be varied through time, otherwise, ρ\rho = 0.8 is inferred.

# library(postie)
# library(malariasimulation)
# 
# mal_sim_output <- malariasimulation::get_parameters() |> 
#   malariasimulation::set_drugs(drugs = list(AL_params)) |> 
#   malariasimulation::set_clinical_treatment(drug = 1, timesteps = 1, coverages = 0.5) |> 
#   malariasimulation::set_epi_outputs(clinical_incidence = c(1,100)*365, 
#                                      severe_incidence = c(1,100)*365) |> 
#   malariasimulation::run_simulation(timesteps = 1)
# 
# mal_sim_output$ft_sev <- 0.5

The severe case fatality parameters can be set directly in the get_rates() function where μH\mu_H and μC\mu_C are set with the hosp_sev_cfr and community_sev_cfr arguments, respectively.

Adaptation from the Griffin (2016) calculations

The original Griffin-2016 calculations hard-wired the shortcut to refactor severe cases and mortality, where all malaria deaths were simply taken as 0.215 times the modelled incidence of hospital‑treated severe case. We have replaced this with an explicit two‑stream calculation that first separates severe episodes into hospital and community compartments, then applies setting‑specific case‑fatality ratios to each stream. A new column, ft_sev, lets users supply (and vary over time) the proportion of severe cases that reach hospital. A warning‑backed default of 0.8 preserves backward compatibility - when this default is used the original 0.215 (based on the default parameterisation) deaths‑to‑hospitalised‑cases ratio is recovered.

Derivation of the 80% hospitalisation for reference

Let:

  • μH\mu_H = severe case fatality hospital: 0.065

  • μC\mu_C = severe case fatality community: 0.6

  • λH\lambda_H = severe incidence hospital

  • λC\lambda_C = severe incidence community

  • νD\nu_D = scaling factor linking hospitalised severe incidence to total malaria deaths: 0.215

Total deaths (predicted two ways) are:

μHλH+μCλC=νDλH \mu_H \lambda_H + \mu_C \lambda_C = \nu_D \lambda_H Solving for the ratio of non‑hospitalised to hospitalised severe cases gives: image

λC=νD−μHμCλH \lambda_C = \frac{\nu_D - \mu_H}{\mu_C}\lambda_H

Coverage (ρ\rho): the share of severe episodes treated in hospital, is therefore: image

ρ=λHλH+λC=μCμC+νD−μH=0.60.6+0.215−0.065 \rho = \frac{\lambda_H}{\lambda_H + \lambda_C} = \frac{\mu_C}{\mu_C + \nu_D - \mu_H} = \frac{0.6}{0.6 + 0.215 - 0.065}

Which = 80%.
